hints: Picture the fatty acid tails in the question, unsaturated tails have kinks from C=C double bonds while hydrogenated tails do not, so ask how straight vs bent tails pack.
Remember that straighter hydrocarbon chains can line up side by side with stronger hydrophobic interactions, so think about what this does to melting point and liquid vs solid state.
walkthrough:
**Recall what hydrogenation does**

Think of it simply like straightening out bent tails. Unsaturated fatty acids have one or more C=C double bonds that cause a kink or bend. Hydrogenation adds hydrogen and removes those double bonds to make them saturated.

**Link shape to packing**

Bent tails cannot pack neatly, so they stay fluid as oils. Straight saturated tails can line up very closely together, which increases London forces between them and raises the melting point.

**Pick the changed property**

So the key change is closer packing of the hydrocarbon chains, which turns a liquid oil into a more solid fat at room temperature. That matches option A perfectly.

options.A: Correct and well done. Saturated straight chains pack closely together, unlike kinked unsaturated chains, so this is the true change after hydrogenation.
options.B: Not true. Both unsaturated and saturated fats are hydrophobic and insoluble in water, hydrogenation does not make them water soluble.
options.C: This is the opposite of what happens. Hydrogenation removes double bonds, so the molecules will have fewer, not more, double bonds.
options.D: This is also opposite. Closer packing raises the melting point, so the fat is more likely to be solid, not liquid, at room temperature.
